findings.message: Scope in and the ownership block say `squatch/config.py` supplies 'the typed configuration hook required by the boundary', but no key, model, or field is named. The boundary described takes its policy, accounting, and dispatch as injected callables and consumes no config value. The implementer would therefore have to invent a config key that no cited plan text specifies. Config models are `extra="forbid"`, so any addition becomes a new public schema key: a speculative knob, which the no-accretion rule refuses. In the section 20 registry, config belongs to the `dispatch-config-snapshot` successor, whose job is the config snapshot.
findings.paved_road: Remove `squatch/config.py` from Scope in, the ownership `hooks`, and the Scope fence, and leave all config work to `dispatch-config-snapshot`. If the boundary truly needs a config value, name the exact typed field (key path, type, default) and the plan text that grants it.

findings.message: Acceptance criterion 4 ('existing config loading and validation behavior remains unchanged and the config hook is limited to the typed input consumed by the dormant boundary') cannot be verified. The hook it limits is never defined, and 'existing config behavior unchanged' is already covered by `tests/test_config.py` under `uv run pytest -q`, so a duplicate proof inside the admission test adds nothing checkable.
findings.paved_road: Drop criterion 4 together with the config fence entry. If a named config field is kept instead, replace the criterion with a concrete assertion about that field's type, default, and refusal behavior.

findings.message: Section 20 requires every continuation to check predecessor-test closure. The criteria only prove that tests/test_scheduler.py stays fenced. scheduler-activation hooks squatch/daemon.py, which will already have the tests/test_daemon_admission.py and tests/test_daemon_config.py tests from dispatch-admission-boundary and dispatch-config-snapshot by authoring time. Those tests may carry dormancy or negative assertions that production activation invalidates. Neither test is in the scheduler-activation fence, and no criterion requires tests/test_seeded_phase3_05.py to prove that activation invalidates no unfenced test. The predecessor phase3-continue-04 did state this general closure criterion.
findings.paved_road: Add a criterion in the same form as phase3-continue-04: tests/test_seeded_phase3_05.py proves predecessor-test closure, so no scheduler-activation fence path invalidates an existing test assertion (including tests/test_daemon_admission.py and tests/test_daemon_config.py) unless that test is also fenced. Keep the Definition of rejected stop for the case where closure needs a path outside the registry fence.
